subject: Getting p-value for correlation between variables

messages.author: d9eaff325339cbcf
messages.subject: Getting p-value for correlation between variables
parts:
Hi all, 

I'd like to get the correlation between variables and its corresponding p-value. Below is my example syntax:

model <- '
# measurement model
ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
dem65 =~ y5 + y6 + y7 + y8
# regressions
dem60 ~ ind60
dem65 ~ ind60 + dem60
# residual correlations
y1 ~~ y5
y2 ~~ y4 + y6
y3 ~~ y7
y4 ~~ y8
y6 ~~ y8
'

fit <- cfa(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy)
summary(fit, standardized=TRUE)

# Covariances:
#                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
# .y1 ~~                                                                 
#   .y5                0.624    0.358    1.741    0.082    0.624    0.296
# .y2 ~~                                                                 
#   .y4                1.313    0.702    1.871    0.061    1.313    0.273
#   .y6                2.153    0.734    2.934    0.003    2.153    0.356
# .y3 ~~                                                                 
#   .y7                0.795    0.608    1.308    0.191    0.795    0.191
# .y4 ~~                                                                 
#   .y8                0.348    0.442    0.787    0.431    0.348    0.109
# .y6 ~~                                                                 
#   .y8                1.356    0.568    2.386    0.017    1.356    0.338

My understanding is that the Std.all column presents correlations (i.e., standardized solution) between the variables, and to get the corresponding p-value, I need to run this additional syntax:

standardizedSolution(fit, se = TRUE, cov.std = TRUE,) %>% filter(op == "~~")

#      lhs op   rhs    est.std         se         z       pvalue    ci.lower  ci.upper
# 1     y1 ~~    y5 0.29576095 0.13969844 2.1171386 3.424809e-02  0.02195704 0.5695649
# 2     y2 ~~    y4 0.27256678 0.12035125 2.2647606 2.352737e-02  0.03668266 0.5084509
# 3     y2 ~~    y6 0.35622239 0.09654540 3.6896877 2.245295e-04  0.16699687 0.5454479
# 4     y3 ~~    y7 0.19064093 0.13315379 1.4317349 1.522197e-01 -0.07033570 0.4516176
# 5     y4 ~~    y8 0.10880178 0.13076853 0.8320181 4.053987e-01 -0.14749983 0.3651034
# 6     y6 ~~    y8 0.33777086 0.10971929 3.0785003 2.080453e-03  0.12272500 0.5528167

giving that the correlation between y1 and y5 is 0.296 (identical to what's presented under Std.all column in the model summary) and this correlation is significant (p=.034). 

Just wanted to check 1) if this is the right way to obtain the correlation and its corresponding p-value, and 2) if I can use this same syntax for obtaining the correlation between observed and latent variable.

Thank you!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Getting p-value for correlation between variables
parts: the correlation between y1 and y5 is 0.296
No, it is the correlation between their residuals.  Is that what you are looking for?
if I can use this same syntax for obtaining the correlation between observed and latent variable.

Only if the correlation/covariance is an estimated model parameter could you get a p value for it(s standardized value).
